about: Statements typed by hand from public sources on rendezvous in the geostationary belt by Chinese, United States and commercial satellites, one statement per source per pair of objects. The stages are as in leo.json; in the belt the plane is shared, so beside, closest and left are the stages stated. Never derived by a program.

statements.ref: Victoria Samson, "Chinese Military and Intelligence Rendezvous and Proximity Operations" fact sheet, Secure World Foundation, 12 June 2026, p. 3

beside.stated: circumnavigated Chinasat 5A at 50 to 100 km for several days, closing to within a few km on 30 November 2016

closest.stated: slowly closing in to within a few km on November 30

left.stated: The two satellites remained close until December 29, when AGI reported that Chinasat 5A was drifting away

statements.quote: The SJ-17 made several small maneuvers to circumnavigate Chinasat 5A at a distance of between 50 to 100 km for several days, slowly closing in to within a few km on November 30, before returning to a 50 to 100 km standoff distance.
statements.note: CSIS's SJ-17 repository: rendezvous 12 November 2016, proximity operations 13 November to 28 December. AGI on X, 29 December 2016: Chinasat 5A departed, drifting 0.9 degrees a day westward; SJ-17 remained at 163 E. The few km is typed as 3.

statements.ref: Thomas G. Roberts, "Unusual Behavior in GEO: SJ-17", CSIS Aerospace Security Project data repository, last updated 1 September 2022
